speaker: Doctor
text:
The blood work shows low hemoglobin with a normal MCV and a low reticulocyte count, suggesting the bone marrow isn't responding well; has your infant been exposed to any infections, medications, or has there been a history of jaundice or pale skin? Also, do the apnea episodes seem to occur during feeding or sleep, and does your baby look flushed or blue during these events?

REQUEST TEST: Reticulocyte_Hemoglobin_Content
REQUEST IMAGES: Peripheral_Blood_Smear

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Reticulocyte_Hemoglobin_Content: 29 pg (normal range for infant: 26-31 pg); Peripheral_Blood_Smear: Images show normocytic and normochromic red blood cells with no visible inclusions, schistocytes, or target cells.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The reticulocyte hemoglobin content and smear confirm a normocytic, hypoproliferative anemia without signs of hemolysis or infection; has the infant been exposed to any viral illnesses, and do the apnea episodes involve color changes like cyanosis?

DIAGNOSIS READY: Congenital Dyserythropoietic Anemia Type II (Diamond-Blackfan Anemia) with associated apnea.
